LNMU Internship Rules.Published LNMU Guideline / Operational R: LNMU Undergraduate Internship Guidelines cover UG programmes in constituent and affiliated colleges, including BA/BSc/BCom and vocational/professional/self-financed programmes.
For BA, BSc and BCom, the published guideline specifies 4 credits in Semester V; ordinarily during summer break between Semester IV and V.
120 hours total (30 hours per credit); minimum 90 hours with the Internship Providing Organisation (IPO); remaining time for report preparation, assessment and evaluation.
Each student completes the internship individually; group internships are not permitted.

Physical/on-site is the default. Online/virtual may be completed through government organisations/platforms such as SWAYAM Plus or another government-institution platform, depending on work and with college approval.

Government departments, registered NGOs/societies, firms, industries, research labs, HEIs, local industries/businesses, health sectors, panchayats/municipalities, media organisations and other registered institutions.
Internship should relate to the student's area of study or interest and help develop new skills.
Internship Report 70%; Presentation/Viva-Voce 30%; minimum 45% in each component.
IPO completion certificate within 10 days of completion; report to department within 20 days; marks/award roll within 7 days after evaluation/viva.
Consent letter, acceptance letter, IPO completion certificate, departmental certificate and internship report are part of prescribed annexures.
LNMU's implementation circular states that mere submission of certificates without actual work engagement with a recognised organisation under proper supervision will not be treated as valid.

The April circular excludes unethical/prohibited activities, network-level marketing using personal contacts/social media, alcohol/smoking promotion, religious sect/personality promotion, gambling/illegal activities, and political party/election campaign promotion.
